name: io.github.lookproof/lookproof-mcp
title: Lookproof DNS, mail and TLS security checks
description: SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS, DNSSEC, TLS and DNS checks. Free API key or pay-per-call (x402).

tools.name: mail_check
tools.description: Use when the user asks about mail setup or why mail goes to spam (no reputation, content or blocklist checks). Returns MX, SPF, DMARC, DKIM (your selectors) and a spoofing category. One domain per call; domain_health (needs an API key) adds DKIM discovery and MTA-STS. Ex: 'Check example.com'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: spf
tools.description: Use when the user asks if a domain's SPF record is valid, why a sender fails SPF or if it hits the 10-lookup limit. Returns the include tree, all qualifier and lookup counts. For the IP ranges use spf_flatten. Ex: 'Is the SPF of example.com valid?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: spf_flatten
tools.description: Use when the user asks which IP addresses or servers may send mail for a domain, or to flatten SPF. Returns every IPv4 and IPv6 block the record authorizes, with the include it came from. Analysis only. Ex: 'Which IPs may send mail as example.com?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: dmarc
tools.description: Use when the user asks about a domain's DMARC record itself, or why reports do not arrive. Returns policy, subdomain policy, pct, alignment and report addresses with findings. For a spoofing verdict use spoofable. Ex: 'What is the DMARC policy of example.com?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: dkim
tools.description: Use when the user asks whether the DKIM key for a known selector is published and valid. Returns key type, size, testing and revoked flags with findings. Unknown selector: use dkim_discover. Ex: 'Check DKIM selector1 for example.com'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: dkim_discover
tools.description: Use when the user asks whether a domain has DKIM but no selector is known. Tries 31 common selectors and returns each key found with type, size and flags. None found is a hint, not proof that DKIM is missing. Ex: 'Does example.com use DKIM?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: mta_sts
tools.description: Use when the user asks about MTA-STS or whether inbound mail is protected against TLS downgrade. Returns the record, the fetched policy, mode, max_age and MX coverage, plus the TLS-RPT record. Ex: 'Is MTA-STS set up for example.com?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: tlsrpt
tools.description: Use when the user asks only about TLS-RPT (SMTP TLS reporting). Returns the _smtp._tls record and its report addresses, with findings. For MTA-STS use mta_sts, which includes TLS-RPT. Ex: 'Where do TLS reports for example.com go?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: mx
tools.description: Use when the user asks which mail servers a domain uses or why it cannot receive mail. Returns MX hosts by preference with addresses, null MX and implicit MX. Provider name: mail_provider; reverse DNS of the servers: domain_health (needs an API key). Ex: 'What are the MX records of example.com?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: spoofable
tools.description: Use when the user asks whether someone can send email pretending to be a domain. Returns protected, partial, monitoring, unprotected or broken from the DMARC policy, with gaps. Describes the policy; it does not prove forged mail gets through. Ex: 'Can someone spoof example.com?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: bimi
tools.description: Use when the user asks why a brand logo does not show in inboxes, or about BIMI. Returns the BIMI record, logo and certificate URLs and whether DMARC is enforced as BIMI requires. The logo is not downloaded. Ex: 'Is BIMI set up for example.com?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: mail_provider
tools.description: Use when the user asks who hosts a domain's email (Google, Microsoft 365...) or which services send for it. Returns providers matched from MX hosts and SPF includes, with evidence. For raw MX records use mx. Ex: 'Who handles email for example.com?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: spf_parse
tools.description: Use when the user pastes an SPF record to explain or check before publishing. Returns mechanisms, qualifiers, syntax errors and the number of DNS-lookup terms. No DNS lookups; for a live domain use spf. Ex: 'Explain v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

tools.name: dmarc_parse
tools.description: Use when the user pastes a DMARC record to explain or check before publishing. Returns p, sp, np, adkim, aspf, rua, ruf and unknown tags, with the same findings as dmarc. No DNS lookups. Ex: 'Explain v=DMARC1; p=none'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

tools.name: email_headers
tools.description: Use when the user pastes email headers and asks why a message failed SPF, DKIM or DMARC, went to spam or arrived late. Returns the Received hops with delays, the verdicts, domains and alignment. Offline; addresses masked. Ex: 'Why did this email fail DMARC?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

headers.description: The header section of one email as text (Received, Authentication-Results, From ...); the body may be left out.

tools.name: dns_lookup
tools.description: Use when the user asks for the current public DNS records of a name, e.g. to confirm a change. Returns A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA, CAA or SRV records with TTL and the resolver that answered. No PTR (reverse DNS) lookups. Ex: 'Show the TXT records of example.com'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

name.description: The DNS name to look up, e.g. _dmarc.example.com.

types.description: Optional record types, comma-separated: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA, CAA, SRV (default A).

tools.name: dnssec
tools.description: Use when the user asks whether a domain's DNS is secure or DNSSEC-signed, or why it fails on validating resolvers. Returns secure, insecure, bogus or unknown with DS and DNSKEY details. For name servers see nameservers, for certificate rules caa. Ex: 'Is the DNS of example.com secure?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: caa
tools.description: Use when the user asks which certificate authorities may issue SSL certificates for a domain, or why issuance is refused. Returns CAA issuers for normal and wildcard certificates and iodef, from parents too. Ex: 'Can Let's Encrypt issue for example.com?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: nameservers
tools.description: Use when the user asks which name servers a domain uses, who hosts its DNS (from the NS names) or whether they are redundant. Returns the NS set with addresses (up to eight); flags a single server, unresolvable ones, one network and missing glue. Ex: 'Which name servers does example.com use?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: rdap
tools.description: Use when the user asks for a domain's whois or registration data: when it expires, the registrar, or if it is locked. Returns registrar, creation, change and expiry dates, statuses and name servers from RDAP. No contact data. Ex: 'When does example.com expire?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: tls_certificate
tools.description: Use when the user asks to check a site's SSL/TLS certificate, why HTTPS fails or when it expires. Returns trust, name match, expiry, issuer, chain, key and TLS version for port 443, with findings. Ex: 'When does the SSL certificate of example.com expire?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: security_headers
tools.description: Use when the user asks which security headers a live website sends or if it forces HTTPS. Returns the redirects from http:// and https:// and HSTS, CSP, frame protection, Referrer-Policy and cookie flags. Ex: 'Which security headers does example.com miss?'. Free trial without an API key: a few calls a day.

domain.description: A public domain name, e.g. example.com.
